Q: In LiPo batteries, how does the number of cells in series change the total voltage when they're fully charged?
A: When you connect LiPo battery cells in series, each cell adds its voltage to the total. Since a fully charged LiPo cell is 4.2 volts, if you have two cells in series (2S), the total is 8.4 volts when fully charged, three cells (3S) would be 12.6 volts, and so on. Q: In ESC control modes, how does using default throttle control versus active speed control affect how accurately I can track motor RPM?
A: When you use default throttle control on an ESC, the signal you send is just mapped to a percentage of power delivered to the motor—so if you set 50% throttle, the ESC gives about half the possible voltage, and the actual RPM can drift due to changes in load or battery voltage. But with active speed control, the ESC tries to keep the motor spinning at a specific RPM you set, which means it can track and maintain motor speed much more accurately, even if conditions change. So, active speed control gives you much better RPM tracking than just using throttle.

A: When flying a drone, some of the biggest invisible hazards are electromagnetic interference from things like power lines, cell towers, and even dense clusters of Wi-Fi or Bluetooth signals in urban areas.
